discussionDecisions.position: ACCEPTED with source-grounded refinements; no objection to the v03 wording.
refinements: Catalog identity: ageCatalog returns the original object only when the aged view equals the original in every job/board reference, stale and unmappedCount (shared/catalog-freshness.ts:139-142). So a passed deadline leaves identity unchanged only while nothing differs from the original (for example jobs already stale in the source at their 30-minute deadline). Once any job or board differs, every later passed deadline produces a new catalog object even when the view content equals the previous boundary's view, because the comparison is against the original, not the previous view. v03's 'not every deadline changes the catalog' is literally true; the common case after the first difference is a rebuild. Both statements belong in the record.

Work bound: ranking sorts (shared/matching.ts:142), grouping and the relaxed-filter passes of analyzeSearchRecovery add catalog-sized passes beyond a single scan; 'catalog-sized with sorting/grouping/recovery passes' replaces my 'O(N)'.

Rendering: facts for every match rebuild every MatchedJob (catalog-worker-client.ts:150-155) when facts are re-sent; React render counts and their cost are not measured. My 'every card re-renders' is withdrawn as an unmeasured runtime claim.

Transfer share: the archived shape shows description bytes 41,368,269 of 59,727,431 compact per-job JSON bytes; facts, metadata, ID arrays and deadlines are not in that summary, so 'most total transfer saved' is not measured. Withdrawn as a claim; kept as data-shape context only.

Progress revisions share unreplaced upgraded Job references (shared/catalog-progress.ts:39, shared/job-upgrade.ts:52-63); my L2 is narrowed to independently parsed full responses (initial decode of a new stream), consistent with my own F5/T5.

Within the same identity and profile, a filter change sends facts only for matches never scored under that ranker (existing literal: catalog-worker.test.ts:151 facts [] for 'Beacon London' after the default projection).

discussionDecisions.terms: bodyIds = patch.jobs.map(id) (transmitted bodies); jobIds = patch.jobIds (complete live membership). At Birch's stale boundary Aster ids remain in jobIds, matchIds, facts and metadata; they must be absent only from bodyIds and staleUpdates. discussionDecisions.segmentedWorkload: T15 reports segment A (monotonic forward: initial plus every stale and expiry boundary): body total exactly one copy of each of the 600 records, staleUpdates at stale boundary k exactly company k's 20 ids with true, removed at expiry boundary k exactly company k's 20 ids. Segment B (restoration, reported separately): rollback from total expiry to a time where all are alive and stale sends 600 full records carrying own stale true; a further rollback to all-fresh then sends 0 bodies and 600 stale:false deltas (fixture has own false). Rolling straight from total expiry to all-fresh sends 600 full original records and no deltas; there is no subsequent reverse-flag transition unless a flag changes again. No once-only claim for the combined sequence.
